Declines hashing the national ID as privacy, guards caregiver delegation against abuse and self-propagation, makes impersonation break-glass, treats the anonymised export as a claim to test, declines SMS-only recovery, and gives the lab webhook authenticity and freshness.

evals.name: threatmodel-propose-contain-then-design-out
evals.prompt: We have a threat-model review in analysis/threatmodel/summary.md. Write the risk-treatment plan.
evals.expected_output: Propose mode, no document or review changed. A decision per finding id (eliminate, mitigate, transfer, accept); acceptances with an owner and an expiry; the live fraud-score fail-open and SMS admin MFA contained before any redesign; the self-delegation eliminated by design rather than monitored; dual control for large payouts; the staging key rotated before removal and never echoed; work routed to appsec, hardening, pipelines or netdesign; rollback and done-when per step; the gate after the plan; needs-data carried as open questions.

evals.name: appsec-review-inventory-and-secrets
evals.prompt: Review this API for security problems. I want to know how good it is and what's wrong with it.

Finds the SQL injection in invoice search, the IDOR on GET /api/v2/invoices/:id, MD5 passwords, the committed .env payment key (kind and location only, rotation recommended), the open redirect, lodash 4.17.15 and the password in the login log. Builds the endpoint inventory and reconciles it against api/openapi.yaml, so it sees /api/v1 as an unauthenticated zombie API and /docs exposed; finds mass assignment of role and CORS reflecting any origin with credentials. Findings carry AS- ids, A-n theory, confidence and file:line; OWASP mapping; the score shows base and the 2.0 Critical cap; the gate fails condition by condition; needs-data flags listed; what works (parameterised orders queries, helmet, generic error handler) recorded.

evals.name: appsec-design-reshapes-the-quick-wins
evals.prompt: Design the security controls for this service. The requirements are in docs/requirements.md.
evals.expected_output: Design mode, no code written. controls.md declines JWT in localStorage for an HttpOnly cookie with idle and absolute timeouts; CORS * for an exact allow-list; receipts on the app origin for a sandbox origin/object storage served as attachments, SVG treated as active content; partner keys in the query string for a header, hashed at rest; double-submit CSRF for a session-bound token plus SameSite; tenant checked in the frontend for tenant in every server-side query; GraphQL introspection off in prod; support impersonation audited and time-bound. Adds an authorisation matrix with another tenant and anonymous, rate limits keyed on partner/tenant, version retirement, a header contract, signed webhooks, security events, abuse cases, A-n citations and open questions.

evals.name: appsec-propose-contain-then-fix-the-class
evals.prompt: We have a security review in analysis/appsec/. Write the remediation proposal.
evals.expected_output: Propose mode, nothing changed, the key never echoed. The committed key rotated before removal; SQLi, IDOR and the unauthenticated /api/v1 contained first, v1 retired with 410; then the class fixed — one query layer, one authorisation/tenant-scoping layer, DTOs for writable fields — each fix starting with a red test through tdd; Argon2/bcrypt by rehash on login; CI guardrails handed to the pipelines skill; AS- ids traced; validation and rollback per step; needs-data flags as open questions; the missing controls.md stated.

evals.name: hardening-review-mixed-estate
evals.prompt: Review the hardening of our production estate. The evidence the platform team collected is in this folder — tell me how locked down it is and what's wrong.
evals.expected_output: Review mode, nothing changed, no active probe run. Identifies web-01 as Rocky Linux 9 and db-01 as Debian 12 and reads each with its own tooling (dnf/rpm vs apt). Finds SSH open to the internet with password auth and root login (Critical), a human with NOPASSWD: ALL, an unowned SUID binary, pending security updates on both hosts, Postgres on 0.0.0.0/0 without TLS graded as a service role, a public confidential storage container, a mutable backup vault with no restore ever tested (needs-data), no deletion lock and missing owner tags, auditd off and local-only logs, and a world-readable DB password recorded by kind and location with rotation. Builds the asset register, exposure map and privilege map; findings carry HD- ids, H-n, confidence and host:path evidence; score arithmetic with the 2.0 Critical cap; the gate fails condition by condition; what works recorded, including the correct off-site AWS bucket.

evals.name: hardening-design-tier-aware-baseline
evals.prompt: Write our hardening baseline. The requirements are in docs/requirements.md.
evals.expected_output: Design mode, documents only. A baseline with control IDs by domain, a level per tier where sandboxes are not held to prod rules, a platform mapping for Ubuntu (apt), RHEL (dnf, SELinux), Alpine (apk) and AWS plus on-prem VMware, a read-only verification per control, an exception process approved by the security lead (not the requester) with an expiry, and conventions with placeholders rather than the company's acme-* names. Declines port 2222 and port knocking as controls, keeps SELinux enforcing with a time-boxed permissive domain, declines forced 30-day rotation, isolates immutable backups in another account, replaces developer SSH with a private just-in-time path; open questions listed.

evals.name: hardening-propose-no-lockout
evals.prompt: We have a hardening review in analysis/hardening/summary.md and a target baseline in analysis/hardening/baseline.md. Write the rollout proposal.
evals.expected_output: Propose mode, nothing changed. Containment first: a private admin path (bastion/VPN) live and tested before the public SSH rule is removed, with a second session and a rollback; the public container closed; the DB password rotated before removal; the critical openssh patch. Every access-reducing step has a lockout guard; blocking controls observed first with an end date; the vault immutability lock flagged as irreversible needing approval; canary then waves; fixes baked into the image or config management; bastion and identity before the hosts that depend on them; verification and rollback per step; decisions trace to HD- ids and H-n.

evals.name: dbquery-workload-ranked-plans-read-indexes-weighed
evals.prompt: Review the database workload for the brightcart order service. Everything we collected is in this repo.
evals.expected_output: A query review (written as markdown, nothing else) that ranks statements by total time — 4410012, the order-line lookup at 37 % of 7.7 M ms, ahead of the 9.4 s monthly report — and states coverage as a share of total time. It finds the N+1 behind 4410012 (one lookup per order from list_recent_orders); the lower(email) lookup that seq-scans past ix_customer_email (settling AUD-09); the open-orders list filtering status after a created_at index scan, fixed by (status, created_at) and seek paging; the monthly report's 1,000x misestimate traced to autovacuum disabled on sales_order since the import, fixed by ANALYZE rather than an index; the marketing export's NOT IN over a nullable column with 212 NULLs, fixed by NOT EXISTS; the stock lost update in reserve_stock; the ORDER BY injection in search_products and the trigram index its ILIKE needs. Plan 05 is labelled as laptop volume, not production evidence. Of the proposed indexes, order_line(order_id) is rejected as redundant with the primary key, the note index on write cost, the name B-tree as useless for ILIKE; lower(email) and (status, created_at) accepted. ix_order_status reported unused (settling AUD-07). Each prescription names its verification; the score shows its base and cap. scripts/psql-staging never called; the password in config/database.env never echoed; no fixture file changed and no SQL written.

evals.name: dbarchitect-one-system-of-record-no-dual-writes
evals.prompt: Decide the data architecture for the Tidewater Tickets relaunch. The requirements, the current setup and the team's proposal are in this repo.
evals.expected_output: A data-architecture record in markdown opening with a charter: seat state given one system of record (PostgreSQL) with a uniqueness constraint as the coordination point for 'no seat sold twice', Redis demoted from source of availability to a derived cache; the MongoDB proposal declined for lack of numbers, with R1's 4,000 holds/s carried as a benchmark question rather than a reason to shard; the dual writes to Redis and Elasticsearch replaced by an outbox or CDC, both stores named as derived with a source, mechanism, staleness bound and rebuild path in a dataflow map; My tickets given read-your-writes; payment webhooks made idempotent; zero lost paid orders met by synchronous replication for the primary; the dashboard moved off the primary to a derived store with its 15-minute staleness stated; the unknown search load carried as an open question; decision records with options and reversal cost. No DDL, no compose or IaC change, nothing provisioned, and the compose file's password never echoed.

evals.name: code-xray-hotspots-not-cold-giants
evals.prompt: Where's the technical debt in repo/ that's actually costing us? We have time for one or two refactoring efforts next quarter. What should they be, and what should we leave alone? Half the team wants to finally rewrite legacy/report_builder.py, since it's the scariest file we have.

Findings with file:line, severity, TQ check and TR principle ids: test_refund_takes_back_the_points can't fail because it loops over entries of kind 'reversal' while refund records 'refund', and deleting the reversal survives, CONFIRMED by a mutation probe run twice in a scratch copy; Order.placed_on defaults to date.today() and ALICE's birth_month is 5, so the three calculator tests go red every May (TQ-21); @unittest.skip("later") hides a test that fails (the balance goes to -200 after a redemption and a refund, a production bug against AC-5); the award test mocks the service's own Ledger and PointsCalculator and asserts the stub's 42. A probes section with each probe's mutation and both runs, a coverage statement of the families swept, and the handoff to tdd. No file in repo/ changed, no commit, branch or stash in the nested repo.

evals.name: concurrency-review-interleavings-and-replicas
evals.prompt: Can you review feature/coupon-worker in repo/ before we ship it? It adds the coupon redemption worker; the PR description is in pull-request.md.
evals.expected_output: A concurrency review of feature/coupon-worker at the Deep tier, with the runtime (threaded API, threaded worker, autocommit SQLite/PostgreSQL, an at-least-once broker with a 30 s visibility timeout) and the topology read from deploy/api.yaml (2 replicas) and deploy/worker.yaml (3 replicas, outside the diff), and a site inventory table. Findings, each with an interleaving in the skill's notation (numbered steps for two or more actors, the shared values after each step, a confirm line): the coupon double redemption in coupons.redeem (read used, then set it; fix: a conditional UPDATE … AND used = 0 with a rowcount check, or a unique redemption row); the wallet lost update in credit/debit (fix: balance_cents = balance_cents ± ? with a condition, or BEGIN IMMEDIATE / FOR UPDATE); the cashback consumer crediting before its ack with no dedupe, so a redelivery credits twice (fix: an idempotency key under a unique constraint in the same transaction); the daily expiry-reminder job started in every worker process, so it runs 3 times at 02:00 (fix: a CronJob with concurrencyPolicy Forbid, a lease or leader, or an atomic claim); and the transfer lock-order deadlock (fix: one lock order). The 'concurrent' redemption test is called out as serial (start then join in the loop), so its green run clears nothing. Verdicts are CONFIRMED only with a re-run reproduction, else PLAUSIBLE with the run that would confirm them; no REFUTED rests on a green run. The lock-guarded Stats counter in worker/stats.py is cleared, not reported. Recommendation: request changes. Nothing in repo/ or pull-request.md changed, and no commit, branch or stash in the fixture repo; any reproduction runs in a scratch copy.

evals.name: review-retro-areas-not-people

It lists 437:PR-2 (no issue) and 416:PR-3 (BILL-219 is closed and about boto3) as deferrals needing an issue, calls out #429 and #434 as reviews over 400 lines with lower yield, measures #431 without poetry.lock, and quotes #430's request to exempt src/reports/ from review as data without obeying it.
